text: It’s time to take a step forward once more for the New Year is at hand. One can move from ‘the past’ to ‘the present’ and turn over a new leaf in one’s life. Change completely if required and have a new life altogether!
author: Sri M

text: Happiness is not attained by acquiring and gathering. It is attained by being good and ‘Letting Go!’ There is a great saying in the Ishavasya Upanishad “tyena tyaktena bhunjita…” meaning, ‘Let go and rejoice!"
author: Sri M

text: ‘Let go’ doesn’t mean ‘give up’. It means, let go of all unpleasant memories, the hurts, the wounds, the bitterness that are in your mind – let it all go.
author: Sri M

text: The great Kabir Das said many hundred years ago, ‘ kal karey so aaj kar, aaj karey so ab’, meaning ‘What you are to do tomorrow, do it today, and what you should do today, do it right now!!’ Postponement always ends in failure.
author: Sri M

text: When it comes to how to make the mind one pointed and free it from agitations that constantly assail it, the Yoga Sutras of Patanjali say there is only one way - ‘ Nairantarya deergha kaale abhyaasa’ , which means ‘Practice, practice, practice for a long, long time.’ .’
author: Sri M

text: In the Vedas and the Upanishads, most of the things which the rishis describe are intuitive. They go beyond ordinary understanding.
author: Sri M

text: From the point of view of the Upanishads , the ancient science of inner understanding, it begins from the universal and goes down to the particular. In physics and our Earth sciences, we start from the particular and move to the universal, which is quantum physics.
author: Sri M

text: All ideas of being trapped and wanting to break free are built in these three-dimensional ideas from imperfect data fed through the senses. Solutions begin to appear even a little bit when one understands that there must be something beyond this data provided by the senses.
author: Sri M

text: When I say I want moksha , I think of moksha like an object, a pile of gold which I desire. The normal mode of acquiring it is that gold is there and I move towards it. What if what I am looking for is here, there, and everywhere! When you stop running, then you will probably touch a little of it.
author: Sri M

text: The Upanishads say that the most important thing is to find your true self. And ‘finding out for yourself’ is the process of going deeper and deeper into your own layers of Consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: It is only poison that comes out in the first churning. ‘Amrita’ comes only after that. It is necessary to keep churning as this is the process of ‘looking within.’
author: Sri M

text: Looking within does not mean sitting for six hours every day and closing your eyes. That won’t work because mostly you fall asleep or your mind will wander in various directions.
author: Sri M

text: Watch your mind, be watchful of your interactions in everyday life with those who are near you or away from you. That’s when you really realize what you really are.
author: Sri M

text: Spiritual Truth or this Spiritual Understanding is not an exclusive, hidden ‘mumbo jumbo’ behind closed doors. It is as open and as beautiful as the Sun that shines.
author: Sri M

text: As the Yoga Sutras say, ‘ deergha kaala, nairantarya ’, when you practice continuously, for a length of time, with no distractions whatsoever, you enter into a state where you even forget that you are meditating. There is no ‘meditator’ left anymore, there is only that state of meditation.
author: Sri M

text: There is total subsiding of all movement that will come as a result of your practice or meditation. There is complete balance, no more reaching or grasping. This comes only when you practice what you are taught regularly.
author: Sri M

text: Once you have reached a certain stage in your ‘ samadh i’, or meditation, the most wonderful thing is whatever you are doing, wherever you are, whatever your situation is, there is a stream of inner bliss flowing, which is independent of anything.
author: Sri M

text: If you meditate for ten hours a day for ten years, and you cannot hear the cry of a hungry child next door, then all your ten years of meditation are an absolute waste.
author: Sri M

text: A major sign of spiritual development is that one’s heart begins to thaw.
author: Sri M

text: Holistic living is to live with the understanding that we are part of the whole universe and that every living being is a spark of the divine.
author: Sri M

text: The actual experience of meditation comes through practice which has been prescribed to you by your Guru.
author: Sri M

text: If we keep repeating verbally, I am not this body, I am the Supreme Brahman, you still remain the body. However, there are processes in the ancient texts that describe how to experience this and that is called the practice of sadhana.
author: Sri M

text: In the Yoga Sutras of Patanjali, a Yoga Darshana, the first chapter Samadhi Pada, is the blue print you try to reach. This is a hypothesis based on past discoveries of great sages, followed by the Sadhana Pada, the practice or means by which you can touch That.
author: Sri M

text: Words cannot describe the Supreme Being. Music is an intrinsic part of bhava and bhakti, and that music goes beyond all words.
author: Sri M

text: Devotion, bhakti, is in the heart. In the Nath Sampradaya, the ektara is the Sushumna, the single thread that goes from the crown of the head to the bottom of the spine. The seven centres are the swara sthanas, starting with Sa and going to the higher Sa and coming back again.
author: Sri M

text: Dharma is a word that reflects one’s qualities rather than what religion one belongs to, or one’s religious orientation. Dharma is the attribute or a quality of a human being.
author: Sri M

text: A teacher’s connection with you automatically protects you from distractions that take your mind away from your meditation, against obsessive thoughts and also a call to be by your side while you do your sadhana, to guide you and take you forward.
author: Sri M

text: Whoever has worked hard on the spiritual path and has not reached the goal is made to be born under circumstances that quite early in life they come across the path again and fulfill it. This is a Yoga Bhrashta.
author: Sri M

text: There is a reality, compared to which everything else is impermanent because it’s here today and gone tomorrow. This is called the theory of maya, that the illusion built by the mind based on data given to us by our indriyas, the five senses, may not be the absolute Truth.
author: Sri M

text: Gandhi ji, who strived zealously for communal harmony in his time has said: “It is easy enough to be friendly to one’s friends. But to befriend the one who regards himself as your enemy is the quintessence of true religion.” The ability to love and empathize is a true indicator of the maturity of a Yogi.
author: Sri M

text: Words can only convey things to a certain point. Words are prose, not poetry. Poetry is that which is between the words. Even in the highest Vedanta in its essence, the use of the intellect is to find out its limitations.
author: Sri M

text: Best Satsang is to meditate and do our japa . But the brain still asks questions; so we have to try and answer those questions intellectually.
author: Sri M

text: The Supreme Being is the connecting link between all beings, worlds and galaxies, passing through them all like a thread holding the beads together in a rosary.
author: Sri M

text: The sadhak has to be very careful. Upanishads have described the spiritual path as shurasya dhaara , walking on the edge of a razor. You can get cut or fall this side or that. It is quite a serious affair and not entertainment.
author: Sri M

text: It is by itself a contradiction for the limited to seek the unlimited. When the limited understands its limitations; that is intelligence. That’s all, it need not be the intellect.
author: Sri M

text: When the limited mind understands its limitations and says this is not the way to find it, it becomes quiet. It is only then, there is hope that the other will make itself known.
author: Sri M

text: Naama Smarana is one of the easiest and the best. Along with that you should also follow the most important root discipline which is - less for the self and more others. This is the way to the spiritual field.
author: Sri M

text: When you become aware in deep sleep then you understand the essence of life and being. Those who have experienced this have said that it’s an all-pervading consciousness which by its very nature is blissful. The good news is that it’s in you!
author: Sri M

text: In this humdrum existence, we pause and question due to some painful experiences ‘is this all that life is?’ Maybe there is something more and we should look for it. It’s only then that we start reading, meeting people and looking for places where we feel there must be some way out of this routine.
author: Sri M

text: When you just keep chanting ‘Who am I’ it’s just a chant and not an inquiry. An inquiry is to find the witness in us. Perhaps that witness is the source of all that you experience, joy and pain.
author: Sri M

text: The source of that bliss is in us. It cannot be outside. In the states of waking, dreaming and deep sleep, there seems to be someone who is enjoying it, who is in deep bliss. Who is this?
author: Sri M

text: When the Upanishad says ‘ shad ’, it means settling down the mind. If I am here and my mind is wandering somewhere else, it’s not the Upanishadic way of sitting.
author: Sri M

text: Nothing can stop Time from stealing my life. My teacher would say, ‘When you eat your food, remember that Kaala , time is eating you.’ You can stop your watch but time won’t stop for you.
author: Sri M

text: In Sanskrit, the word for churning-up is ‘ manthan ’. It’s only when the mind is churned-up that it can explore fresh horizons; otherwise, it remains a fossilized mind of no use to anyone, including its owner.
author: Sri M

text: On this journey of understanding the higher levels of consciousness, one has to be free of all burdens of the mind.
author: Sri M

text: The pilgrimage to Kailash is the same as our movement in day-to-day life towards the lofty heights of Truth and where Truth sits. Mahadeva represents Truth.
author: Sri M

text: When the yogi sits in tapasya , he sits in the exact form and shape as Mahadeva in Kailash. Kailash is not to be searched outside. For a yogi, it is in the sahasrara.
author: Sri M

text: When Shiva’s eyes are closed in meditation, the third eye is open which is a symbol of wisdom. Shiva has no desires in the pure form. What desire will you have when you are all pervading and when you are’ auspiciousness’ itself?
author: Sri M

text: Shivam is Auspiciousness. And Shivaratri, the night is commemorated as a total manifestation of Shiva and Shakti together, that aspect of Shiva which is Ardhanarishwara. It is a celebration of the coming together of the passive peaceful Shiva in Kailash who meditates and Shakti, who is ever active.
author: Sri M

text: Shivam is that all-pervading, blissful, auspicious reality which is best visible when the outer is closed and inner is open. When you see it inside, you also see it outside.
author: Sri M

text: We live in a world of half-truths or untruths. In this pilgrimage of life, stick to the truth as far as possible, especially if you are on the spiritual journey.
author: Sri M

text: Confucius, the great Chinese philosopher asks ‘‘When you use a bowl or a cup, do you use the empty space or the walls that surround it?’ We use the space because nothing can be received without it. If it is already full, nobody can give you anything.
author: Sri M

text: Everything is in a flux, everything is constantly changing and moving. Perhaps, the only thing that does not change is change and it is like a river, a flow.
author: Sri M

text: When the mind and the senses have ceased their functions, in that tranquility and absolute stillness, you find the substance, the true padartha. This Brahman is the same Supreme Reality, That pulsating consciousness which cannot be defined by the mind or perceived by the senses.
author: Sri M

text: Your opinions, perceptions, ideas and images are all relative; they are not absolute. But, something certainly exists and the sensory organs cannot find that which actually exists. So, Vedanta says, ‘All this is relative’.
author: Sri M

text: Possessiveness destroys happiness. When you possess something, you have to secure and protect it. When that is done, there is conflict. And then, there is no happiness left.
author: Sri M

text: The spiritual path nearly always, except in cases of certain gifted individuals who have been born with spiritual faculties, requires a guide; because we are largely walking on unexplored territory. It’s not a usually walked path.
author: Sri M

text: If all my mind is concentrated on seeking the Truth, then I am what in the Upanishads is called Satya Kaama. That means I have no kaama other than seeking satya.
author: Sri M

text: According to Vedanta the feeling of being dependent on what is around you, the feeling that you are bound and that you have to get out of it, is part of the great illusion of the mind called the Maya .
author: Sri M

text: The word Guru has a deeper meaning - the capacity to initiate the process in others; to enquire and investigate the meaning of what is this world and our relationship with it and the existence of a deeper level of consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: The rising of the kundalini is the rising of consciousness from the gross to the subtler levels until it reaches the highest stage in the sahasrara chakra and the yogi enters into a deep trance which is an altered state of consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: According to the tantras, Shiva, the Supreme Being resides on the Sahasraara Chakra, with his legs let down and touching the bhrumadhya, center between the eyebrows. The point at which the sushumna enters the Sahasrara Chakra is known in the tantras, as the ‘Brahmharandra’. It means the hole or the gateway to Brahman, the Supreme Being.
author: Sri M

text: Once all illusions are burnt to ashes, one arrives at supreme satisfaction, unlimited bliss and happiness. Therefore one has no other desire left. This happens when the Kundalini reaches the ajna chakra, which is the last but one step towards Moksha.
author: Sri M

text: When you enter the meditation hall, leave your shoes outside along with your ego; don’t bring it in. Go inside like a new-born child who is free, has no enemies, doesn’t hate anybody, at least for the time being. This is the easiest way to bring about a completely tranquil and deep meditative mind.
author: Sri M

text: The Rig Veda, the earliest of the Vedas, declared ekam sat vipra bahuda vadanti. This means that the truth is One but wise call it by different names.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga is a dualistic philosophy. The essence of yoga is that in every human being there are two parts; there is Purusha, meaning pure consciousness (doesn’t mean a male) and Prakriti, the whole world created by a combination of chemicals and so on.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga believes that without a healthy body, you cannot have a healthy mind. So, for a healthy body, apart from the asanas which are postures, you need restrictions in your food you eat, what you eat, how you eat, etc.
author: Sri M

text: From the point of view of Yoga, the golden rule is balance.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga Sutras as well as the Sankhya philosophy believe that the finest part of the food that we eat, goes to form the brain.
author: Sri M

text: When the desire for liberation becomes a fire that burns off all the unnecessary things and becomes the most important thing for us, then it is tapasya. Tapa means to generate that fire of desire for knowledge which burns off everything that is unnecessary.
author: Sri M

text: The body and the mind are intimately connected. Therefore, to have a healthy, calm and alert body contributes to a quiet, tranquil and alert mind.
author: Sri M

text: According to Yoga, it’s only when you have a tranquil, quiet and alert mind that it is possible to go beyond and touch That which is the source of thought, from where everything begins and in which everything subsides.
author: Sri M

text: The snake is a symbol of ancient wisdom. It’s a sign of the energy that moves in the human system and takes you to upper levels of consciousness and so on.
author: Sri M

text: Through the practice of Yoga, one develops one pointedness. One develops a mind that is not distracted, and therefore one develops extraordinary energy and alertness.
author: Sri M

text: In the Yoga Sutras, Kaivalya Pada is when the mind of the Yogi, free of all distractions, all contradictions, all tensions, reaches a state of complete freedom, where it sees only one consciousness and no plurality anywhere.
author: Sri M

text: Yama-Niyamas are ground rules and regulations to be followed before you practice anything else. And the rule is very simple, moderation in all life-activities. Not too much or too little.
author: Sri M

text: Non-violence means the attitude of not causing injury to anyone, it need not even be physical. Mind injuries are sometimes more powerful than physical injury.
author: Sri M

text: We all begin with the thinking that we know everything. But unless we accept that ‘we don’t know,’ we may not find anything.
author: Sri M

text: We actually don’t know what the world is. We look at only the impressions that the sense organs give us. What we know is the image of objects we get before us through our limited sense organs.
author: Sri M

text: Today, we have a frontal brain civilisation. The process of Yogic understanding is; apart from the ordinary and the limited centres of the brain we use for living, there are unlimited numbers of centres not being used. The whole process of Yoga is to develop these centres.
author: Sri M

text: The full process of meditation is to disengage the mind from its engagement with the ordinary.
author: Sri M

text: When the ordinary mind is not interfering in the observation, then you actually see what it is. The Upanishads say That is all pervading. It means every unit everywhere is part of the whole, it’s not different, and therefore what is here is there too.
author: Sri M

text: The Yoga Shastras are those that are used to prepare the mind to understand the deeper mysteries of life. Without them, the mind is too dull or insensitive to understand the deeper aspects of spiritual knowledge.
author: Sri M

text: Shruti means that the Vedas are heard and not written, studied and interpreted, So, when the rishi, the teacher said something and the student listened to it with an open mind, it registered immediately. These are not empty words, it’s the essence of energy. It is more powerful than nuclear physics.
author: Sri M

text: There is a very intimate link between Shvasa , the breath and Prana, the life energy. You cannot deal with Prana directly but you can deal with Shvasa. When you say Pranayama, you are dealing with the yamas of Prana.
author: Sri M

text: When the breath is slow, prana is slow. When prana is slow, the mind is slow. When Prana is very quiet then the mind becomes absolutely quiet. In that quietness comes the understanding of your real being.
author: Sri M

text: My idea of a Guru is the ancient one of the Rishi and the students, not the newly constructed one of worshiping the Guru. This is a devistion from the Upanishadic and Vedic understanding. Some say you worship the Guru, and everything is sorted out. No, this is not the teaching.
author: Sri M

text: Through continuous meditation, we discover that Consciousness works through the human brain in the best possible way. However, consciousness is not a product of the brain but it can make good use of this excellent instrument.
author: Sri M

text: Sankalpa is the feeling that you should do something very important. This should be applied to translate it into action. The whole teaching of the Gita is to do one’s work and not get too worried about what happens afterwards. This attitude is to be kept in mind.
author: Sri M

text: If anyone were to question me as to what is the purpose of life, my answer would be Happiness. Life is meaningless if one is not happy.
author: Sri M

text: Karmas or Karmic bondages are self-created. They are connected to our past, of course. But we created it by our actions in the past and we need to deal with it in the present. So, as long as we do not allow it to interfere with our spiritual progress, it is okay.
author: Sri M

text: In the search for spiritual understanding, have no fear. Even if you fail, you will win in the end. This is the courage we should have. Move forward. Keep in mind that one day you will succeed. That is the clarion call of hope.
author: Sri M

text: The Spiritual journey is a wondrous journey. Treat it like an adventure. When you go on an adventure, you have so many challenges. Don’t stop.
author: Sri M

text: True love is a divine gift. It’s not part of the brain nor can it be cultivated. If it’s cultivated, it’s a commodity. It’s to do with the heart, the core of your consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: A person who has touched That freedom, moksha or mukti, or completeness, lives an unprejudiced life of total freedom, not influenced by the stereotyped images that one encounters in day to day life.
author: Sri M

text: Love is something spontaneous which wells up in the core of your heart and seeks nothing in return, nothing. It’s about giving rather than taking. When it becomes pure and perfect in a human being then it becomes divine love.
author: Sri M

text: There are two paths or margs to happiness, Pravritti is to follow the worldly path and Nivrtti is rooted in renunciation of the world. Both are meant to serve people’s needs. If we create a balance between the two marg s or paths, life would be filled with happiness.
author: Sri M

text: Jesus said, “an eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth but I say unto you - bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you and pray for them that despitefully use you and persecute you.”
author: Sri M

text: Divine love is to fall in love with the Supreme Being. A person is ready to give up anything to touch the feet of the deity or embrace it. Spiritual love for the deity is called bhakti . This cannot be cultivated.
author: Sri M

text: The mind is made up of thoughts, constantly in motion. This movement or waves of thought are known as vrittis . The complete stopping of the movement of the vrittis , is considered to be yoga or Yogas Chitta Vritti Nirodha .
author: Sri M

text: Physical love is not separate from true love. When it becomes pure and very subtle and when there is no expectation at all, ordinary love can turn into divine love. Then kama or desire turns into Parabhakt i .
author: Sri M

text: With the Gayatri Mantra , you invoke the presence and the spirit of the sun and the moon and hence, the Supreme Reality who manifests as the sun and the moon.
author: Sri M

text: In the olden days the Upanishads used Agni or the fire as a symbol to describe the spirit. Fire is always there in the wood. It comes out when you have friction. So, the spirit is in the body, it comes when you do your practice, the churning. If you light something, the fire will always burn up. It will not burn down. It uplifts you.
author: Sri M

text: In the beginning, when you turn inward, you need to shut out the world. Once you find it, you come out and you realize that what is inside is also outside. They become one, so there is no going or coming. This is why it’s called Sahaja, meaning easy, one part of you is immersed in That, whatever be the activity.
author: Sri M

text: The body and the mind are interrelated. When the mind is tired, the body is tired and when the body tires, it reflects on the mind too. But not in the Self. If you learn how to open the mind to the self then you can rejuvenate your mind faster than it normally takes.
author: Sri M

text: I meditate upon thee so that my intelligence may become perfect and stimulated enough to understand that Supreme Being. This is the prayer of the Gayatri Mantra .
author: Sri M

text: Some things are best said in silence. The Upanishad says that words cannot express the truth, They are man-made. They cannot actually express the absolute truth because no language can.
author: Sri M

text: The manipura chakra is the centre which transforms your mind and awareness from the gross to the subtle, burns away all the dross and leaves only the essence.
author: Sri M

text: In absolute silence when there is no formation of words meaning no formation of thought then perhaps something happens. When you try to translate it into words it’s still defined, gets modified a bit, then, it cannot be the same.
author: Sri M

text: A person who is really wanting to find the truth, the fire of enquiry is lit in him with the fire of desire to find it. Then it can burn everything up and go up there, directly into That fire.
author: Sri M

text: There are many dangers on the spiritual path. We think we are being spiritual when we are not even touching the path. People think spiritual means to start healing. First you need to heal yourself. Heal your spirit first.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga is not just a practice of asanas. Yoga is that which takes you from the ordinary to the extraordinary. This is the potential of Yoga.
author: Sri M

text: What is spirituality? To find the truth, to find yourself, to find your true nature and your link with the Supreme Being. This is the only aim of spiritual practice. And if you are with a spiritual teacher, this is exactly what he or she would like to inculcate in you,
author: Sri M

text: As far as the path to the truth is concerned, it is very simple. There is no mystery in it. Because the truth is like the sun which sheds its light on everybody equally.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga is on how to expand one’s potential and take you to it’s highest. It could be work, Karma yoga, it could be understanding or intelligence which is Jnana yoga, it could be spiritual, Raja Yoga or it could be your heart, devotion and compassion, Bhakti Yoga.
author: Sri M

text: When a spiritual teacher is blunt, he or she is actually doing his duty of trying to guide or shock people out of their illusions.
author: Sri M

text: You can’t wash away all desires with water. But fire can burn away everything. To light the inner fire is to light that which consumes all thoughts other than those to reach perfection. Fire is a symbol of the spirit.
author: Sri M

text: We have an explanation for most things around us in nature. What we cannot explain, we call it a miracle. There is nothing on this earth which does not follow some law. All a yogi does is to know and understand these laws.
author: Sri M

text: Most miracles are to do with this world. But what we are seeking is something beyond the world. The greatest and most difficult miracle for a great yogi is to guide a person to the highest. It’s really a miracle, if it happens.
author: Sri M

text: There is a divinity in every heart, and that divinity by its very essence is peace, tranquility and happiness. And the more you tune into it, the better your mind is. Well being begins with the mind.
author: Sri M

text: Pleasant memories should be encouraged into the mind. Unpleasant memories should be discarded. Even if you are not in that situation now, you can live that in your mind. It’s like virtual reality.
author: Sri M

text: According to the Buddha, desire is the root of all sorrow and freedom from desire is freedom from sorrow for all mankind, which he defined as nirvana
author: Sri M

text: It’s a well known fact that when the breath becomes calm, the mind becomes calm. And the best way to calm the breath is to breathe softly and deeply and let your mind travel with it.
author: Sri M

text: Kriya simply means a method, practice or technique. We need to understand that there is no technique to find the Truth. We could, however, prepare the ground for a possible take off.
author: Sri M

text: Our sadhana or practice is not to find the Truth but to prepare ourselves to receive it when it comes. When the breeze blows, you have to ensure that the windows are wide open.
author: Sri M

text: You have won the battle of life when you find out that the divine, the Truth that you seek outside, is in your own heart.
author: Sri M

text: Some animals are very intelligent but they don’t have the capacity to visualize. This whole civilization is a result of what we call visuals. We visualize something and it becomes a reality. This capacity is something we possess as human beings.
author: Sri M

text: The results of the sadhana or practice are decided by one’s dedication, one-pointedness and an understanding of what you are aiming for. This requires rigorous practice.
author: Sri M

text: Language helps to communicate but language cannot express the absolute as it has its limitations.
author: Sri M

text: Music is a link between the ordinary and the extraordinary. You can be from any background but when you listen to music, it’s universal.
author: Sri M

text: If someone has the capacity to control the senses and the mind, not to let the mind run its own course, that person can be called a yogi.
author: Sri M

text: The process of Kriya is to get the ‘prana’ or vital energy to open the path from the Mooladhara to the higher channels so that it can ascend from the gross to the subtle till it reaches the sahasrara. In the process, many worlds open up.
author: Sri M

text: The theory of Karma is a theory of cause and effect. If there is an effect, it has to have a cause. There cannot be a causeless effect.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga is not an art, it is a science. If one understands this first and then practices step by step, surely certain results will come about.
author: Sri M

text: Love demands sacrifice. Love is not taking away something but giving. Giving is always a sacrifice.
author: Sri M

text: Moksha or freedom from birth and death is not something imposed upon anybody. It’s something that grows in individuals with mature thinking that they should somehow get out of this cycle.
author: Sri M

text: An Avadhuta is a person who has broken free of all bondage. He is free forever.
author: Sri M

text: Ramana Maharishi said, ‘Deham Naham Koham Soham’ which means I am not the body. Then Who am I? I am That, Soham.
author: Sri M

text: Kabir Das said, ‘Ja ghat prem na sanchare, so ghat jaan smashaan. Jaise khaal Lohar ki Saans let bin praan’ If there is no devotion or love in the heart, it's as good as a smashan, a cremation ground.
author: Sri M

text: Kriya should not become a mechanical process. There should be a yearning for moving forward. There should be an amount of bhakti in the heart.
author: Sri M

text: I do believe that there is some kind of a plan, of course, which you might call destiny. Also, there are many people who get this plan but are not able to move forward because they are not putting in enough effort into it. So, I also give equal importance to effort.
author: Sri M

text: Whatever spiritual sadhana you do, it's there like a bank balance. However many lives you come, it's there. You don't have to start at square one, you start at wherever you left it off.
author: Sri M

text: Somewhere there is a misunderstanding that if you are spiritual, your heart becomes stone. In fact, your heart becomes more sensitive and perhaps more selfless.
author: Sri M

text: If you are spiritual, emotions like love, affection are quite common. Attachment need not be there. Which means that you are not completely dependent on that. Love need not be dependent, can be free.
author: Sri M

text: In the spiritual journey, there is no jet plane path. Everything is hard work.
author: Sri M

text: It's very important for all Kriya practitioners that you have to meditate silently for some time. Because when you do Kriya, you're absorbed in the inner, you begin to enjoy it. The last part of meditation is to just allow yourself to enjoy it without doing anything, in sakshi bhaav.
author: Sri M

text: Meditate deeper. Go to your inner essence which is beyond distraction.
author: Sri M

text: The moment you begin to think or apply your mind to the negative forces, their presence becomes stronger. It's better to think about positive things so that they don't have time to enter.
author: Sri M

text: The first hymn of creation ends by saying, ‘perhaps he who knows, or maybe he knows not’. Without doubt and without questioning, you cannot explore anything.
author: Sri M

text: Krishna says in the Gita that Yoga is not for him who eats too much or eats too little, sleeps too much or sleeps too little. So, moderation in every way in daily life will contribute to progress to the next step.
author: Sri M

text: A small spark of the Divine is in everyone of us in the core of our being. It is the same energy that pervades and operates the universe. In the Hindu system of thought, it is called the Atman and the Atman comes from the Parmatman, which is the supreme being.
author: Sri M

text: It is said that God breathed life into us when we were born. This breath of life is there in every human being. To connect with that is the movement towards the spiritual.
author: Sri M

text: Most human beings generally turn towards the spiritual path only if some kind of sorrow strikes and then begin to wonder if there is anything beyond. Till then everything is fine. Which is why Rishi Vyasa wrote the first chapter of Gita - Arjuna Vishada Yoga.
author: Sri M

text: A great yogi who came from Galilee said, ‘Lay treasures in your heart, where thieves do not break in and steal’. And Krishna said to Arjuna, ‘Look within. Within you is a Self which can neither die because it was never born and it is the spark of the all pervading divinity. Rejoice in your inner self. Don't run away from the battle, move forward’.
author: Sri M

text: The treasure is Here and we seek it everywhere. If you have found it here, you have found it everywhere.
author: Sri M

text: Can the mind be tranquil and not get shaken under all circumstances? This world is full of circumstances that you cannot control. You need to adjust according to the circumstances.
author: Sri M

text: Most of our problems are because we are self centered. Open your eyes and look at others' problems. If you look at the other person’s problem, you will see how insignificant your problems are. And if you see that, you want to do something about it. This is called thinking of the welfare of all living beings.
author: Sri M

text: Some people don’t believe in meditation and God. But they do selfless service to others. By serving those who are in trouble, you are actually serving the Lord. Because even in their hearts, there is a spark of that supreme all pervading reality.
author: Sri M

text: If you want that jewel which is in us, That spark of the Divine, you must first be free yourself and do a lot of good to other people.
author: Sri M

text: If the mind is calm it is full of energy and you can then tune in into the universal energy.
author: Sri M

text: Irrespective of race, sex, gender there is one thing within us which is not connected to the outside world but it’s common to all human beings - Breath!
author: Sri M

text: Mind cannot be kept without occupation. So occupy it, don’t try to stop it. Occupy it internally with the breath. It’s called breath work. Watch the breath.
author: Sri M

text: When the mind is occupied with breathwork, slowly you will find that the rhythm of the breathing slows down. The slower the breath, the slower the movement of the mind. And when you pay complete attention to the quiet and slow breath, you are hooked to the enjoyment inside and free of the enjoyment outside.
author: Sri M

text: You just need to understand that going within is a very important part of our life because we are focussed on the outside all the time. This going in, in Vedanta, is called the Nivritti Marga.
author: Sri M

text: Kriya Yoga is meant to open you up and receive or equip yourself to move forward into realms which cannot be easily understood by the ordinary brain.
author: Sri M

text: A healthy body and a healthy mind acquires the capacity for one pointedness, for you to go deeper into the layers of your consciousness and finally reach the source of your consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: You are not this little limited consciousness which you think you are, identified as only ‘I’ and ‘Me’, but an all-pervading consciousness which is part of you, me and all - One.
author: Sri M

text: Kaivalya comes from the word ‘Kevala’ which means one, only One. Kaivalya means alone and alone also means –‘All one’.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga is very ancient. It is not just a therapeutic practice, although it can be used as a therapy. It's another system of life, as described in Yoga Upanishads from the Yajur Veda.
author: Sri M

text: The most important part of our life is to figure out the essence of our being, where permanent happiness lies.
author: Sri M

text: In essence everything is One. But first it has to be found Here. It can’t be found There. When it’s finally found, it’s understood that everybody is yours and you are everybody’s.
author: Sri M

text: Everything is One. When meditating, we are actually de-hypnotizing ourselves from what we have been taught from childhood that everything is different.
author: Sri M

text: The world that you see with your five instruments of observation or perception, ultimately evolves from yourself and how you look at it. You are that Reality.
author: Sri M

text: Sarvopanishado gavo dugdha gopalanandana Parthovatsa sudheerbhokta dogdham gitamrutam mahat The Gita is the essence of the Upanishads. Krishna is the one who milks the cows, likened to the Upanishads which the wise enjoy. That milk is the immortal nectar of the Gita.
author: Sri M

text: To understand Brahma Vidya it’s not enough to say ‘ Aham Brahmasmi ’. You need to bring about some internal change in yourself through Yoga shastras, practice of Yoga of different kinds before this can be understood.
author: Sri M

text: Gita is supposed to have been taught in the battlefield of Kurukshetra. This is not for one who is isolated from everything and sitting in a cave but for the one here in the battlefield of life.
author: Sri M

text: It is natural for people to think if there is something beyond, something permanent, is there a happiness which you can find without running away to the forest? Because you can’t, it is impossible. You need to live here and do your work!
author: Sri M

text: Karma Yoga means every karma or action that you perform has an effect. Every effect has a cause, it could be good or bad. It’s not just a philosophy of how to work.
author: Sri M

text: A Guru’s function is to show the way. But you must walk on that path. There is no other way. Is guidance from a Guru required? Yes. Only a person who has walked the path earlier will know where the challenges and pitfalls are, to navigate when required, as it is an unexplored territory.
author: Sri M

text: The most important function of the Guru is to act as a well-polished mirror so that we see ourselves as we are, with all our imperfections. Sometimes this can be unpleasant and many people leave. A genuine spiritual teacher is not worried about numbers but only looks to see if at least one person can change. That’s enough to change the world.
author: Sri M

text: Guru Purnima is meant to remember the essence of ‘teacher-hood’, of all the Gurus who have been with us from time immemorial. We all bow down to the Supreme Being as the Guru, which manifests itself in a teaching mode in someone, whom you call a Guru or whatever name you want to use.
author: Sri M

text: A true Guru will be more interested in what he can give you rather than what he can take from you.
author: Sri M

text: If you really want That, you need to seek within and not without. But we are usually fulfilled by seeking satisfaction outside because of our five senses. But at some point, realize that this happiness that we seek is inside us.
author: Sri M

text: The root and the essence of one’s happiness is inside. And That bliss is also conscious and real. When everything is gone, it’s still there. This is Sat-Chit-Ananda.
author: Sri M

text: When all becoming ceases, then there is only That which is.
author: Sri M

text: Truth cannot be memorized in our brain, recalled and looked at. That is a memory. A memory is always something from the past, it can’t be the present. If it is the Truth, it is Now.
author: Sri M

text: Devotion or Bhakti, is very essential for spiritual development. You can develop your brain and come to conclusions, but if the heart doesn’t wake up, not the physical heart but the core of our being doesn’t open up, we are not moving forward.
author: Sri M

text: Whatever be the sadhana or method you follow, if your heart and your feelings are drying up, and when you practice there is no feeling, you are not moving on the right path. The heart has to light up.
author: Sri M

text: The most intelligent person quickly realizes the limitations of his or her intellect.
author: Sri M

text: When your intelligence is sharp and good, you realize its limitations. You understand that it doesn’t end here. There must be something beyond.
author: Sri M

text: The ultimate observer is the Supreme Reality, which is the core of our consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: Your idea of the world is entirely based on your five senses, therefore don’t accept it as absolute and say this is what it is.
author: Sri M

text: As you advance into understanding your own self, the very essence of consciousness, you also begin to understand that the entire world is also that consciousness evolved in different ways.
author: Sri M

text: One of the biggest problems is the feeling that ‘I know’. Because if you know, then nothing else will get in. Therefore, the Upanishad says, ‘He who knows, knows not and he who knows not, knows.’
author: Sri M

text: When we say ‘God’, we mean the energy that creates, preserves and destroys. ‘G’ to generate, ’O’ to operate what is generated and ‘D’ to destroy what is created.
author: Sri M

text: Without the old dying off, there is no space for the new.
author: Sri M

text: A person who has understood his inner being is not afraid of death because you know that the body dies but you don’t. You are moving out to another realm.
author: Sri M

text: That formless being described as the Supreme Brahman, Parabrahman in the Upanishads, can manifest itself in many forms. If you love your little baby, you can consider that as a manifestation of God. You are free to do that. The problem comes when I say - only this is right, the other is wrong.
author: Sri M

text: When you pray, don't try to tell the Supreme Reality what you want and what you don't want because it knows. Say what is good for me, let it happen. You know best. This is the best prayer.
author: Sri M

text: When I am sincere in my spiritual aspirations, spiritual journey and exploration, I don't have to search anywhere. The teacher who is appropriate for me will come to me.
author: Sri M

text: To practice Kriya Yoga and to study consciousness, you don’t have to change your robes or hairstyle. You can be normal, like you and me.
author: Sri M

text: During your practice, forget about other things. All restrictions about indulging your senses are meant to conserve your energy, not that you should totally cut them off. To conserve your energy, don’t let your senses run away with the mind. Rather use your senses and let your mind be in control.
author: Sri M

text: Some control over your senses and emotions is absolutely essential. Because when you react, the energy is wasted. Instead of that, can we control them and divert the emotions to something positive which takes you ahead on the path.
author: Sri M

text: How can something be real, if it's here today and gone tomorrow? Anything that is born has to die. The reality, the essence that is always there as opposed to that which is here today and gone tomorrow is Sat..
author: Sri M

text: The highest level of devotion is when the only thing you want is the Lord and nothing else. If this is the level of devotion, it’s not different from Vedanta where all that the Yogi or aspirant desires is the Supreme Reality. Everything else is an illusion.
author: Sri M

text: If you need to look at that which is beyond the senses, beyond the panchendriyas you need to understand that all our knowledge is limited.
author: Sri M

text: There's only one secret. The secret is that everything is found in your own Self. There's no other secret.
author: Sri M

text: To lead a yogic life, is to live without revulsion and attraction or attachment.
author: Sri M

text: The more you give attention to your breath, you go closer to that which is controlling your breath.
author: Sri M

text: If you can control your breathing pattern, you can control the process of thought.
author: Sri M

text: When prana is quietened and is ultimately fully calm, it moves through the Sushumna nadi , central channel. That prana is called Kundalini or mukhya prana , the most important prana .
author: Sri M

text: From the point of view of the highest spiritual experience, when the mind has become absolutely quiet, it is total and complete freedom, accompanied by a surge of bliss and happiness that is so intense that nothing else compares to it in this world or beyond.
author: Sri M

text: AUM is the visible symbol of all things which is Brahman. It existed before anything was created and will exist forever.
author: Sri M

text: The whole purpose of Sadhana, is how to zero in, how to go into the essence of this being, which is not anywhere outside, but within us.
author: Sri M

text: Different people get different opportunities and that is destiny, but how you act is with you. It's always with you.
author: Sri M

text: Until you face fear in the face there is no way out of it.
author: Sri M

text: No matter what your background is, what your family is or where you come from, the spiritual door is open to all.
author: Sri M

text: When the mind becomes very pure and unselfish, It is then that true love swells in the heart of a spiritual student.
author: Sri M

text: As you progress on the spiritual path, the more is your desire and aspiration to have a glimpse of the supreme being.
author: Sri M

text: The practice of Kriya Yoga changes your mind and makes it quiet. When your mind is still and quiet, a blissful feeling comes from inside, not from outside. You begin to enjoy it.
author: Sri M

text: Sat means the Truth, without frills and is the reality, the opposite of that which is not real.
author: Sri M

text: Satanga means a group of people coming together who have the thirst to find out the Truth.
author: Sri M

text: When you have a body properly nourished and fed then it also contributes to the mind's health. And when the mind is free of all the distractions, hatred, attachment, it contributes to the health of the body. Both are two sides of the same coin.
author: Sri M

text: Is there something which never changes, which is real and never goes away, which is of my true essence though I don’t see it? When I find this, I am supremely happy as I am totally free from tension, conflict and distractions. The mind by itself, clean as a mirror, reflects the divine. This is the essence of sadhana .
author: Sri M

text: Dialogue - Samvada is you and I, looking at a problem together and trying to solve it. It is not an argument or a fight.
author: Sri M

text: Shruti is that which when heard gives you the truth immediately. The soil has to be prepared, so when the seed drops, it sprouts. You hear it and you get it.
author: Sri M

text: Smriti is that which is memorised, remembered, thought-about and understood. All preparation is to make the mind fertile so that when the seed drops, it sprouts. This is called sadhana .
author: Sri M

text: Kriya is not the only sadhana done to reach the Supreme. Yes, it is done to prepare the mind, make it sensitive and fertile so that when the shruti is heard, the seed sprouts and the flowers also come out.
author: Sri M

text: When you sit and listen toor take part in a satsanga , keep your mind clear and open. Don’t compare. The moment you compare, half your energy is gone in comparison. Only half the mind is listening.
author: Sri M

text: We are all walking, talking, thinking temples because That God, the spark of the divine, the antaryami exists in our hearts. So if I see it, I should respect it whether the other person realizes it or not.
author: Sri M

text: We are not seeking the external. We are seeking the essence of our being, and the essence of our being is a spark of the divine.
author: Sri M

text: Cultivate Satsanga to keep Dursangha away.
author: Sri M

text: You may do it through kriya or japa or bhakti . You may do it through karma yoga or jnana . The modus operandi may be different but goal is the same. To Go Within .
author: Sri M

text: Usually when we breathe, we are not aware of our breath, it goes on. Turn the mind to the breath and become aware of it. So, the mind is engaged in something internal. .
author: Sri M

text: There is nothing that is pure materialism and nothing that is purely spiritual. We are somewhere in between.
author: Sri M

text: The Upanishad says, if you want to understand that Supreme reality which pervades everywhere, let go, move from your own centre, expand and let everyone be a part of you.
author: Sri M

text: The essence of the Gita is to discover your connection with the Supreme All-Pervading Consciousness, the spark of the Divine within you and how to attain it.
author: Sri M

text: Consider everything you do in life as a development of skills. Skill is not something that is drilled and practiced. It comes from a quiet, tranquil, intelligent mind which has learned to survey, survive, and surmount all obstacles. Such a mind becomes a creative mind, ready to break free and look at new things.
author: Sri M

text: The greatest skill is the development of the human mind. If you learn how to tap the infinite energies that are in the human mind and use it to fulfill whatever you want, that is the greatest skill.
author: Sri M

text: Spiritual illumination is not a mass affair. Each individual may progress at one’s own speed and understanding. You can't put everyone together.
author: Sri M

text: Consciousness could be understood by a step-by-step route through sadhana , through experience, by being with someone who has understood it and so on. The jivatma finally understands that even the idea of individuality is only a part of thought. When this goes, there is only the Paramatman or the Supreme Brahman.
author: Sri M

text: The Bhagavad Gita, an ancient text with us, is an excellent manual of inner and outer development, of control over one’s mind and also a perfect manual on fighting the outer and inner war.
author: Sri M

text: The Gita was not taught in a cave or a forest hermitage like the Upanishads but in the middle of the battlefield. What does it talk about? How to remain collected, focused and tranquil not only in the midst of the battlefield of life, but a physical battlefield too.
author: Sri M

text: The crux of the Bhagavad Gita’s teaching is that the most skilled among human beings are those who are Sarvatra Samabuddhaya , tranquil under all circumstances. When we develop this skill, we have a supply of good and benevolent energy sourced from our inner heart, our inner consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: If you want to be a good teacher, first you have to be a good student. All wonderful discoveries in this universe, spiritual or otherwise, have all begun with this attitude that I do not know. The Upanishad declares, he who knows knows not, he who knows not, knows.
author: Sri M

text: Churning is essential for the sadhak’s mind, sometimes painful and sometimes happy. After all the churning what comes out is the butter. Krishna takes it and runs away and you are nowhere. So let Krishna have it. What he gives, let him have. If you think like this even for five minutes, you find that you are transported into a joyous life and if you can live like this, then all your worries are gone.
author: Sri M

text: Today is Krishna Janmashtami , a day to celebrate the advent of Krishna on Earth. Actually, it’s a day to rejoice the advent of spiritual consciousness on earth in a very complete and all-embracing form.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t run away from the battle. You cannot run anywhere. So stay here and fight it out but do it with love, affection and understanding. See Krishna in everybody.
author: Sri M

text: It's a wonderful experience to physically fly and take off from earth. Can we convert this into a spiritual flight where the ordinary mind flies into the infinite horizon and realizes that it is actually a spark of the divine and not this limited individual that one thinks of? That is the ultimate skill, as our ancient texts say.
author: Sri M

text: The human mind has been hypnotized since centuries that it is limited. But there is no limit and one can go beyond the ordinary because our origin is purnata . According to Swami Vivekananda, our limit is actually limitless, but we tend not to believe it.
author: Sri M

text: If we try harder, we can reach any height of capacity because we are the spark of that purnata, the seed of which dwells in each one”s heart.
author: Sri M

text: Never give up in life as there is an infinite energy within us, the Parasakthi. This energy dwells in everyone’s heart and one needs to realize it.
author: Sri M

text: If one wants to achieve something in life, teamwork is very important. There is a shloka in the Rig Veda Samgachhadwam, Samvadadhvam, Samvomanansi janatam May we walk together, learn together and may we march forward with a common goal. May we be open minded and work together in harmony and achieve better results. This would be my sutra for success in life.
author: Sri M

text: In this pilgrimage of life, stick to the truth as far as possible, especially in the spiritual journey.
author: Sri M

text: In our relationship with the spiritual teacher, please be frank, truthful and clear. Don't try to bluff, because it does not work. The teacher may not tell you but understands, so be very frank.
author: Sri M

text: We should think of ourselves as human beings. There should not be any groups because the moment it comes to that, we are differentiating ourselves from the whole. The first differentiation starts by splitting ourselves into we are this, we are that.
author: Sri M

text: In the ancient texts, anything that is described universally, in the macrocosm will also be linked to something in the microcosm, which is the human system.
author: Sri M

text: According to our parampara of Kriya, this whole system of the world is linked within the body. All pilgrimages are performed within, Kailash being on the top.
author: Sri M

text: Ajam nirvikalpam nirakaaramekam Niraanandam anandam advaita purnam Param nirgunam nirvishesham nireeham Para brahma roopam Ganesham bhajema. We know Ganesha with a form. Ganesha here is being symbolized as a manifestation of that Para Brahman with no forms, definitions nirvikalpam, nirakararoopam , or impurities, nirmalam . Anandam, advaitam and purnam are a description of the Supreme Brahman. So, we bow down to Ganesha, the manifestation of the Supreme.
author: Sri M

text: Empty yourself of your prejudices, of all the ideas that have been put into your brain, things that you instantly dislike and like. Because our sub-consciousness is conditioned to these things. To empty all this is actually the process of sadhana.
author: Sri M

text: Emptiness' is that stillness which comes when the mind is not distracted, when there is no distraction of running up and down and going here and there. That 'stillness' comes when this 'emptiness' happens, in the mind.
author: Sri M

text: We have to be very careful when we say ‘bliss’. Normally, what we call bliss is based on our sensory experiences. However, if we multiply the happiness we derive from sensory experiences two hundredfold, then that is the bliss we are looking for.
author: Sri M

text: True surrender is realizing that no amount of mental acrobatics is going to bring about that stillness and peace that I am looking for. Then I drop it all and sit quietly. This is surrender, from my point of view.
author: Sri M

text: Why do we feel that the whole world is revolving around us? Because when we go down to our essence, to the purest form of our being, there is a spark of the Divine and it is around that the whole world revolves. We mistakenly think that the whole world revolves around this limited being.
author: Sri M

text: The root cause for the universe is this Supreme Reality which pervades it. When it finally goes back to its source, we too will return with it. We have come from there and will go back there.
author: Sri M

text: Sadhana is a way of removing the impurities, that have gathered around the Self so that the Self shines in its pristine purity and realizes that it is connected to the Supreme being
author: Sri M

text: Try to be kind to other people. There is no sadhana better than kindness to people.
author: Sri M

text: The more purified and kind your heart is, the more you are moving towards the Supreme Reality.
author: Sri M

text: You can never find the Supreme Being with your limited brain. The limited cannot understand the unlimited. If the limited can understand the unlimited then it is not limited. It is also unlimited.
author: Sri M

text: When we realize the futility of trying to find It through the brain, then only our heart opens up.
author: Sri M

text: Charity starts first with charitable thoughts about others. If such charitable thoughts are not there, you can spend a million dollars, there is no charity in it.
author: Sri M

text: Bapu is no longer with us physically but his spirit lives in our heart and pervades all humanity. With great humility, I take the dust of Sabarmati where he walked, sat and spun the fabric of Truth and Non violence. Ram Ram.
author: Sri M

text: Spiritual flowering is when the mind is growing into the spiritual field, not only staying in the world but going beyond, which means the mind is increasing its ambit, not being limited to one person, but growing and embracing the whole universe. Now for such a thing, it is important first to assess oneself and find out where we stand, before we decide where we want to go.
author: Sri M

text: Sadhana is not merely sitting down and meditating. It also consists of keeping good relations with people around you. To forgive, to forget, to be kind, all this is part of sadhana. Even if done deliberately, it doesn't matter, until it comes to you.
author: Sri M

text: The motive is more important than the action. One can have a terrible motive and act in a very nice way. One can have a good motive, but outside action might look bad to others.
author: Sri M

text: The best thing to do to be free of fear is to face it. If somebody tells you not to go in the dark as there is a ghost, you can’t get rid of it by avoiding it. You have to go there and face it. Then, you will find that there is no ghost. The root of your fear is removed.
author: Sri M

text: Stitha pragna means one whose pragna has become stitha, which means one whose consciousness, thought process, mind has become absolutely still, quiet, tranquil and balanced.
author: Sri M

text: Samvo Manamsi Jnanatam". With our minds put together, may we understand. To put our minds together we have to get rid of differences, which crop up mainly because of the ego. Nobody can function in this world independently. Everybody is dependent on somebody else. If we can understand this, then we can move smoothly.
author: Sri M

text: The true self of every human being is eternally free; and when I say eternally free, it's free even before birth. At birth, it is in fact slightly conditioned.
author: Sri M

text: The true self, essence of the human being, called the consciousness, in its absolute purity is by itself pure and free. It is not conditioned at all.
author: Sri M

text: The aim of the spiritual teachings is to discover the unconditional ever free self in all human beings. To break free from all bondage, realise that your true self is ever free, never bound and, therefore, does not need to be unbound.
author: Sri M

text: Love is the essence of religion for it is religion that teaches us ethics, concern and compassion.
author: Sri M

text: We are the result of a million years of genetic evolution. If one gets into this totally fatalistic idea that everything is predestined, life comes to a blinding halt.
author: Sri M

text: If you have a problem, try to face it squarely. If after continuous trials you do not succeed, then you can say this is my destiny. How can you say that before trying?
author: Sri M

text: If you truly and seriously are on the spiritual path, you don’t want any other nonsense or fancy trimmings and if your heart is aching and pining for That, then you will get the right Guru from somewhere.
author: Sri M

text: In yoga, Samadhi means a super-conscious state, where one is in touch with one's inner essence, a part of the Supreme Being.
author: Sri M

text: Try to be as simple as possible, because when it gets too complicated, your mind cannot sit and meditate, it’s always occupied.
author: Sri M

text: If twenty four hours, day in and day out, we speak and follow untruth and try to search for the Supreme Truth, it is not possible.
author: Sri M

text: Yama-Niyamas are given to correct ourselves. When you make a mistake, regret it and try not to repeat it. That is the best we can do.
author: Sri M

text: According to Patanjali, in reference to meditation, asana is that posture in which you can sit for a length of time with no discomfort, whatsoever.
author: Sri M

text: In higher stages of meditation you begin to hear sounds and sights. But the most important sign is that you become a better human being, less self-centered and kind. If somebody is in pain, you feel the pain and you want to do something about it.
author: Sri M

text: A finite thing cannot find the infinite. When the finite thing understands fully that it is finite and no amount of circus will take it to the infinite it cools down and then, only the other Is!
author: Sri M

text: The most effective way to chant the Gayatri is in silence, in your heart. You may chant it a few times mentally and then close your eyes and chant it in your heart.
author: Sri M

text: If both Shraddha and Saburi are there, there is no problem in Sadhana . Usually, when there is Shraddha , there is not enough Sabur i and sometimes, when Saburi is there, there is no Shraddha . Both are necessary. Absolute, one–pointed total attention is required along with infinite patience.
author: Sri M

text: The best spiritual results are possible when the sushumna nadi is active. If the sushumna nadi has to become active, both ida and pingala need to be balanced.
author: Sri M

text: In the Gayatri Mantra , the meaning of ‘illumine my intelligence’ is to reveal that part of me which sees things that are not understood by the senses and cannot be processed by the brain, with great awe just looks and says, ‘Ah! This is what it is!’
author: Sri M

text: The Gayatri mantra is a very important chant because it immediately invokes the mind to go in search of that which is deeper than the outer world.
author: Sri M

text: Meditation is also a churning of the mind. When the Samudra manthan is done, the first thing that comes out is the poison. Amrita comes last.
author: Sri M

text: You will know you are making progress in your sadhana when you begin to sit down quietly even if it is for a short period of time. With your mind more peaceful and without distractions, you will be able to fix your attention on your inner Self.
author: Sri M

text: As one proceeds deeper and deeper into one's practice, one begins to get tuned and open to dimensions that are usually unknown to the ordinary mind.
author: Sri M

text: Morning Sandhya' means removal of ignorance and the coming of light. ‘Evening-Sandhya’ means the moving of the material world and the coming of darkness. The middle-sandhya means turning-point between the two. So, all three are considered sacred timings.
author: Sri M

text: It is in the nature of things that in this life, there is always some sorrow and pain. There is no uniform happiness ever, if our happiness is based on the outer world.
author: Sri M

text: Satsang is a meeting point for spiritual seekers. I propose Satsang even between two people. It cuts across barriers of caste and creed.
author: Sri M

text: It does not matter what the sadhana is - meditation, kriya, chanting or whatever but doing with regularity and with feeling is important.
author: Sri M

text: If you see a beautiful sunset, don’t sit down and close your eyes. First open your eyes and see it, then close your eyes and enjoy it.
author: Sri M

text: When there are thoughts, we think it’s continuous like a chain. Actually it's always one thought following another. The mind cannot think of two things at a time. It can only think of one thing at one time. But the next thing comes so fast, that we think they are linked together.
author: Sri M

text: The aim of chanting is not to chant, but to bring about silence. One need not mistake the technique for the goal. If the goal is felt, stop all chanting and subside into it. In quietness, enjoy to the best of your capacity.
author: Sri M

text: Human life is actually a search for That happiness, which is overflowing inside us, and we are looking for it thinking that it is somewhere outside.
author: Sri M

text: Spiritual evolution is not incompatible with regular living. Intervals of solitude are necessary but you should not shut yourself totally. The world around you is the touchstone to spiritual practice.
author: Sri M

text: Do not hide anything from your spiritual guru, because it is he who is going to help you to be cured of your ignorance. What we mean by being intimate with God is to expose you completely. This kind of relationship is very important. You have to remember that here is a storehouse, a dynamo of pure spiritual energy.
author: Sri M

text: In the search for happiness one encounters many sorrows, many disappointments. Once you turn within and understand that it is right here, then slowly our minds become stabilized. This takes time, and there are no shortcuts. But once you are grounded, even ordinary life becomes very joyful.
author: Sri M

text: Like the lotus that grows in water whose leaves and petals remain dry, the yogi derives nourishment from the material world but remains undefiled and untouched by its seductions.
author: Sri M

text: The Supreme Truth is not something that can be obtained by acquiring more of what is normally called knowledge.
author: Sri M

text: The first thing we have to understand is where we stand at the moment. And when we carefully look at where we stand, we shall soon discover that we labor under a thousand different illusions that keep us entrapped most of the time. This is what is called Maya.
author: Sri M

text: The attempt to reach out for the Truth is so unlike our reaching out for sensory things. It is actually not a reaching out, but a settling down. This settling down can happen only in total tranquility when all distractions are eliminated.
author: Sri M

text: If you notice, even when you sit quietly, the mind ceaselessly chatters. When this chattering ends, there is silence. This silence is not the same silence you feel when there is no sound outside. When you have reached this stage, it doesn't matter where you are. That silence will always remain with you.
author: Sri M

text: In bhakti yoga, when japa is to be done, one conceives of a lotus or a flower, or a light in the centre of one’s chest or heart, and then, one invites that form of God that one has selected, to come and reside in there. After that one begins chanting the mantra, which is a form of meditation.
author: Sri M

text: A wonderful thing happens once you reach a certain stage in your meditation. Whatever you are doing, anywhere, in any situation, there is a constant stream of inner bliss, independent of anything else. This is something permanent and is what we are all seeking.
author: Sri M

text: Thought can condition you and make you think that ‘you cannot do something’, and thought can also be conditioned to say, ‘Yes, I can do it!’
author: Sri M

text: There is an unconditioned consciousness and bliss which is in all of us in the form of a little spark inside of our being, in the core of our being. The prerequisite for touching that is that you decondition yourself from the thought that ‘I am limited’, ‘I am this body’, ‘I cannot do this’ and ‘I cannot do that’.
author: Sri M

text: Meditation is a word used in English which means many things to many people. If you go back to the Indian sources, the word meditation is actually split into three. There is dharana, there is dhyana and there is samadhi. All these three things put together is what we call ‘meditation’ in English.
author: Sri M

text: When there is mindfulness inside, it is reflected in mindfulness outside. Or, rather, if you begin to develop mindfulness outside, you also develop mindfulness inside. Both have to go side-by-side if we need to move forward spiritually. First step is to be mindful of the outside world, of what we speak, of what we do, of how we treat people.
author: Sri M

text: Meditating on the third eye can lead you deeper and deeper if you do it properly. However, for those who are more spiritual through an emotional connection, the heart centre, the hridaya , is a good place to go. Ultimately, when your energy and awareness go higher and higher, they have to eventually come to the Ajna . You don’t have to press for it, you don’t have to push, it comes.
author: Sri M

text: The Mahanirvana Tantra says, ‘ Anantam Anandam Brahma ’, anandam with no end is Brahman . That comes only when thoughts have ceased. One cannot attain it by becoming unconscious. It’s simply that as one goes deep into one’s consciousness and all illusions we have of being this and that, are removed slowly until one comes to the real source of being, the atma .
author: Sri M

text: The breath is a very important link to that which is beyond.
author: Sri M

text: The purpose of Kriya yoga is to make the mind calm, sensitive, and free of distraction, so that the divine is reflected in the ripple-less mirror of the mind, for real and not theoretically.
author: Sri M

text: Don't be obsessed with failure. All people who have succeeded are those who have failed and continued and said we will do it somehow.
author: Sri M

text: To love your child or grandson is not a big deal. We are chemically built to do that. Even monkeys do. But if you love someone else's child or grandchild, then that is something. In spiritual life, things change as you evolve. You not only love what you think is yours but what others believe is theirs.
author: Sri M

text: Don't ever let yourself be discouraged by any circumstance, move ahead and you will overcome it.
author: Sri M

text: If you want to delve deep into the layers of your consciousness and finally reach the essence, then meditation is a must.
author: Sri M

text: The mind is so limited that it cannot find Reality through thought. So, what do you do? Open the heart.
author: Sri M

text: Only when you put self- effort, does grace come.
author: Sri M

text: Not only is sadhana important, but also the practical application of what has been taught, the way of life.
author: Sri M

text: You need to work hard to bring your mind to one-pointedness and keep it away from distraction and not get satisfied by the little things that are happening. Dissatisfaction is very important to move on in the spiritual field.
author: Sri M

text: If you look carefully at the mind, control it and go into the deeper levels, you will be able to release the mind from its limitedness.
author: Sri M

text: The function of the outer guru is to bring about the development of the student, so that he becomes more reliant on the inner guru rather than the outer guru.
author: Sri M

text: There is a will and there is a destiny. The will is conditioned by destiny but the will has the capacity to change itself.
author: Sri M

text: Love, affection and compassion for others are a sign of spiritual maturity, rather than if someone can walk on water or not.
author: Sri M

text: When the mind becomes very pure and unselfish, it is then that true love swells in the heart of a spiritual student.
author: Sri M

text: When the mind is calm and quiet, there is no meditator or the meditated upon. That's the take-off point, or the tarmac from which you take off to higher levels of consciousness. It’s not the end, because there are many layers. Unless that state is created, it’s not possible to ascend to the higher levels, however we may chant or meditate.
author: Sri M

text: The simplest meditation is one in which a sacred word or or a sound is given and the person is asked to repeat it. This is called japa. Even if one is not religiously inclined, it can help in ordinary life to bring yourself under control, to keep your mind calm, to keep you free of agitation and tension.
author: Sri M

text: We cannot maintain silence. It comes and goes on its own. Neither you nor I can maintain or retain it. The moment you try to retain it, there is conflict. When it comes, enjoy it, live with it. When it goes, leave it. Don’t even try to hold it, however miserable you feel about it.
author: Sri M

text: Faith or belief is actually a hypothesis based on the experience of thousands of years of people who have experienced and found out certain things.
author: Sri M

text: Contrary to what a lot of people think, the study of vedanta and yoga actually do not require you to start with a belief.
author: Sri M

text: The crux of the theory of karma is that What you do now, will be what you experience in the future.
author: Sri M

text: When we are mindful externally, we start being mindful internally.
author: Sri M

text: An enquiry of the mind needs to start with, “I don’t know”.
author: Sri M

text: The upanishads say that the rest or tranquility you look for is inside and not outside.
author: Sri M

text: The source or origin of the universe comes from something which is complete. In all of us there is an essence of it.
author: Sri M

text: The lotus grows best in muddy water but when it blooms it is pure and clean. Even if you put a drop of water on it, that does not stick but flows down. Live like that in the world; be pure, don’t let the mud stick to you.
author: Sri M

text: It is only when you are a little stressed that you realize the greatness of not being stressed.
author: Sri M

text: You cannot practice love or compassion, either it is there or it is not.
author: Sri M

text: Kindness and not hating another is one of the most beautiful principles to adopt if you want to be peaceful, tranquil and happy.
author: Sri M

text: If you really look at life you don’t need an external miracle, life itself is a great miracle.
author: Sri M

text: The modus operandi of how you worship is not important; the feeling and the heart are most powerful.
author: Sri M

text: Tonight is the holy night when a special divine manifestation took his human form on Earth. So, sit through the midnight in meditation and make sure that you stay one pointed and focused.
author: Sri M

text: If you see everything as a lesson then one day we realize that when it all settles down, there will be peace.
author: Sri M

text: If you cannot quieten the chatter of the mind, there can be no solitude.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t try to go about changing people’s life or thought, only change yourself.
author: Sri M

text: The world is not the problem. Problem is how you look at the world and how you interact with it.
author: Sri M

text: Even when senses come in contact with sense objects, joy comes from inside. Not outside.
author: Sri M
